def deserialize[V2](
    source: Serialized,
    annotation: TypeDef[V2],
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
) -> V2:
    """Deserialize an object from the source type or format.

    Args:
        source: The source object to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.

    Returns:
        An instance of the object, deserialized from the source.
    """
    # Reading is not restricted to lossless formats: the lossiness of a format
    # describes what an export can drop, not what an import can restore.
    candidates = get_serializers(
        annotation,
        targets=[_source_type(source)],
        scope=scope,
        lossless=False,
    )

    if len(candidates) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No suitable serializer found for {type(source).__name__} as "
            f"{annotation!r} under scope {scope!r}."
        )

    _, _, driver = candidates[0]

    if isinstance(driver, type) and issubclass(driver, Serializable):
        return cast(
            V2,
            driver.__deserialize__(
                source,
                scope=scope,
                realm=realm,
                annotation=cast(TypeDef[Serializable[Any, Any]], annotation),
            ),
        )
    else:
        return cast(V2, driver.deserialize(source, scope=scope, realm=realm, annotation=annotation))

    instance: Any,
    target_type: TypeDef[T2],
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Serializable[T2]] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the byte size of serializing ``instance`` to ``target_type``.

    Serializers override this when they can measure their format cheaply. The
    default falls back to :func:`sys.getsizeof`, which measures the object
    in memory rather than the encoded representation.

    Args:
        instance: The object to be serialized.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The estimated number of bytes.
    """
    candidates = get_serializers(
        typ=annotation if annotation is not None else type(instance),
        targets=[target_type] if target_type is not None else None,
        scope=scope,
        lossless=lossless,
        value=instance if annotation is None else None,
    )

    if len(candidates) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No suitable serializer found for {type(instance).__name__} to "
            f"{target_type!r} under scope {scope!r} "
            f"with lossless={lossless}."

        candidates,
        lambda driver, target: (
            driver.__estimate_serialized_size__(
                instance,
                target_type=target_type,
                lossless=target.lossless,
                scope=scope,
                annotation=annotation,
            )
            if isinstance(driver, type)
            else driver.estimate_serialized_size(
                instance,
                target_type=target_type,
                lossless=target.lossless,
                scope=scope,
                annotation=annotation,
            )
        ),
        scope,
        realm,
    )

def get_serializers[U, T: Serialized, S: TransportScope, L: bool](
    typ: TypeDef[U],
    targets: Collection[TypeDef[T]] | None = None,
    scope: S = Open(),
    lossless: L = False,
    value: object | None = None,
) -> list[tuple[int, SerializationTarget[T, S, L], Serializer[U, T, S] | type[Serializable[T, S]]]]:
    """Get the serializers that can handle a given type or instance.

    Args:
        typ: The type or instance to get the serializer for.
        targets: The serialization targets to write to or read from. Instances are
            matched on their MIME type and IO type, so the serializer for the actual
            format wins; types only narrow by class. ``None`` skips the target
            check and returns the serializers for the object type alone.
        scope: The scope to select for. A serializer declared for a supertype
            scope (e.g. Open) also serves a request for a narrower one.
        lossless: When ``True``, only serializers that round-trip the target
            format without loss are eligible; ``False`` accepts either.
        value: The instance to select for. A type alone cannot express element
            constraints — an SQL statement list and ``[1, 2]`` are both ``list`` —
            so a value is validated against the driver's declared object type as
            well. ``None`` matches on the type only, which is what introspection
            wants.

    Returns:
        A list of tuples of the form ``(index, target, driver)``, where
        ``index`` is the index of the matching target in the list of targets,
        ``target`` is the matching serialization target and ``driver`` is the
        serializer or serializable class to handle the object.
    """
    candidates = []

    cls = TypeRef(typ).common_type

    if issubclass(cls, Serializable):
        candidates = sorted(
            [
                (i, t, cls)
                for i, t in enumerate(
                    SerializationTarget.match(
                        cls.__serialization_targets__(), targets, scope, lossless
                    )
                )
            ],
            key=lambda x: x[0],
        )  # Sort by index to prioritize the first match

    if len(candidates) > 0:
        return candidates  # pyright: ignore[reportReturnType]

    candidates = sorted(
        [
            (i, t, driver)
            for driver in custom_serializers + common_serializers
            if _handles(driver, typ, value)
            for i, t in enumerate(
                SerializationTarget.match(driver.serialization_targets, targets, scope, lossless)
            )
        ],
        key=lambda x: x[0],
    )  # Sort by index to prioritize the first match

    return candidates  # pyright: ignore[reportReturnType]

def serialize[T2: Serialized](
    instance: Any,
    target_type: TypeDef[T2] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Serializable[T2]] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> T2:
    """Serialize an object to the target type or format.

    When no target type is given, the serializer picks its preferred format: the
    first one it declares, which is the lossless one wherever it has a choice.
    ``lossless`` therefore only filters the selection once a target is requested.

    Args:
        instance: The object to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The serialized target object.
    """
    candidates = get_serializers(
        typ=annotation if annotation is not None else type(instance),
        targets=[target_type] if target_type is not None else None,
        scope=scope,
        # Without a requested target the driver picks its preferred format, so
        # there is no format to judge: the lossless filter applies only once a
        # target is asked for.
        lossless=lossless if target_type is not None else False,
        # With no annotation the instance itself narrows the selection: a bare
        # ``list`` cannot say whether it holds SQL statements or integers.
        value=instance if annotation is None else None,
    )

    if len(candidates) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No suitable serializer found for {type(instance).__name__} to "
            f"{target_type!r} under scope {scope!r} "
            f"with lossless={lossless}."
        )

    return cast(
        T2,
        _dispatch(
            candidates,
            lambda driver, target: (
                driver.__serialize__(
                    instance,
                    target_type=target_type if target_type is not None else target.type,
                    lossless=target.lossless,
                    scope=scope,
                    realm=realm,
                    file_factory=file_factory,
                    annotation=annotation,
                )
                if isinstance(driver, type)
                else driver.serialize(
                    instance,
                    target_type=target_type if target_type is not None else target.type,
                    lossless=target.lossless,
                    scope=scope,
                    realm=realm,
                    file_factory=file_factory,

@staticmethod
def match(
    targets: Iterable[SerializationTarget[Any, Any, Any]],
    types: Collection[TypeDef[Serialized]] | None = None,
    scope: TransportScope | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
) -> list[SerializationTarget[T, S, L]]:
    """Return the subset of targets that match any of the given types.

    Args:
        targets: The list of serialization targets to filter.
        types: The collection of types to match against.
        scope: The scope to match.
        lossless: Whether to only include lossless targets.

    Returns:
        The list of matching serialization targets.
    """
    return cast(
        list[SerializationTarget[T, S, L]],
        [
            t
            for t in targets
            if (
                any((TypeRef(tt).is_subtype_of(t.type)) for tt in types)
                if types is not None
                else True
            )
            and (_scope_serves(t.scope, scope) if scope is not None else True)
            and (not lossless or t.lossless)
        ],
    )

@classmethod
def lossless_target(cls, hint: TypeDef[Any]) -> bool:
    """Whether a target format round-trips the object exactly.

    A file target does exactly when all of its MIME types are declared
    lossless by the serializer; a target that is not a file follows
    :attr:`__lossless_values__`.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if the target is lossless for this serializer.
    """
    mimes = target_mimes(hint)

    return (
        all(mime in cls.__lossless_mimes__ for mime in mimes)
        if mimes
        else cls.__lossless_values__
    )

def match(self, scopes: Collection[TransportScope | type[TransportScope]]) -> bool:
    """Check whether this declared scope can serve any of the requested scopes.

    The declaration is the receiver and the requests are the arguments: a
    declaration serves a request when the request is an instance of the
    declared scope, so a serializer declared for :class:`Open` serves every
    request, while one declared for a narrower scope cannot serve an
    unrestricted one. Scopes form a hierarchy rooted at :class:`Open`, and
    the comparison is the class relation, never an exact-class match.

    return any(_scope_serves(self, scope) for scope in scopes)

def target_mimes(hint: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return the MIME types a file target declares.

    Args:
        hint: A target type, a :class:`TypeRef`, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The declared MIME types, in declaration order; empty when the hint is not
        a file target.
    """
    if hint is None:
        return ()

    ref = hint if isinstance(hint, TypeRef) else TypeRef(hint)

    for var, value in ref.typevar_map.items():
        if var == M:
            return cast(tuple[str, ...], tuple(value.literal_values))

    return ()

def serialize(
    self,
    instance: Container,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> SerializedDict | list[SerializedValue]:
    """Serialize a container to the JSON-shaped payload it reduces to.

    Args:
        instance: The container to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: Unused; this serializer produces values, not files.

    Returns:
        The dictionary or list the container reduces to.

    Raises:
        UnsupportedTargetError: If a file target is requested, which this driver
            does not produce.
    """
    if file_factory is not None or _is_file_hint(target_type):
        raise UnsupportedTargetError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} reduces a container to a value, not to a file; "
            "serialize the payload to a file target through its own serializer."

        SerializedDict | list[SerializedValue],
        _container_payload(instance, scope, realm),
    )

    self,
    instance: Image.Image,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the uncompressed pixel payload.

def serialize(
    self,
    instance: Image.Image,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,

    """Serialize an image to an image file.

    Args:
        instance: The image to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the target MIME type is not supported.
    """
    target = self._file_target(target_type, file_factory)

    # The encoder comes from the target format, never from the source
    # image: a JPEG loaded from disk must still be written as PNG when
    # the target is a PNG, or the payload contradicts the declared loss.
    image_format = _image_format_for_mime(target.default_mime)
    if image_format is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported image MIME type: {target.default_mime}")

    with target.open("w") as stream:
        instance.save(stream, format=image_format)

    return target

def deserialize(
    self,
    source: NpFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Deserialize an array from ``.npy``, ``.npz`` or CSV.

    Args:
        source: The file to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized array.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the source MIME type is not supported.
    """
    file = _require_file(source, type(self).__name__)

    with file.open("r") as stream:
        if file.default_mime == "application/x-npy":
            array = np.load(cast(BinaryIO, stream), allow_pickle=False)
        elif file.default_mime == "application/x-npz":
            array = np.load(cast(BinaryIO, stream), allow_pickle=False)["arr_0"]
        elif file.default_mime == "text/csv":
            array = np.loadtxt(cast(TextIO, stream), delimiter=",")
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type: {file.default_mime}")

    return check_type_and_cast(array, annotation)

@override
def serialize(
    self,
    instance: np.ndarray,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> NpFile:
    """Serialize an array to ``.npy``, ``.npz`` or CSV.

    Args:
        instance: The array to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the target MIME type is not supported.
        TypeError: If the array holds Python objects.
    """
    target = self._file_target(target_type, file_factory)
    mime = target.default_mime

    # Both checks run before the target is opened, so a rejected array or
    # format cannot truncate an existing file.
    if mime not in {"application/x-npy", "application/x-npz", "text/csv"}:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type: {mime}")

    if mime in {"application/x-npy", "application/x-npz"}:
        _require_native_dtype(instance)

    with target.open("w") as stream:
        if mime == "application/x-npy":
            np.save(cast(BinaryIO, stream), instance)
        elif mime == "application/x-npz":
            np.savez(cast(BinaryIO, stream), arr_0=instance)
        else:
            np.savetxt(cast(TextIO, stream), instance, delimiter=",")

    return target

def deserialize(
    self,
    source: str | SQLFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,

    """Deserialize statements from SQL text or from an SQL file.

    Args:

        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized statements.

    statements = [sqla.text(str(stmt)) for stmt in sqlparse.parse(_read_text(source))]

    # Rebuild the container the annotation asks for; the statement count
    # alone cannot tell a scalar from a one-element list.
    origin = get_origin(annotation)
    shaped: object
    if origin is list or origin is Sequence:
        shaped = statements
    elif origin is tuple:
        shaped = tuple(statements)
    elif len(statements) == 1:
        shaped = statements[0]
    else:
        shaped = statements

    return check_type_and_cast(shaped, annotation)

@override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: SQLStatement,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Measure the formatted statements from a sample.

    ``sqlparse.format`` parses and re-renders every statement, which costs more
    than writing them out; a strided sample is formatted and extrapolated
    instead, the same way CSV output is sampled by row.
    """
    statements = [instance] if isinstance(instance, sqla.Executable) else list(instance)

    total = len(statements)
    if total == 0:
        return 0

    sample = statements[:: _sample_step(total, _SQL_ESTIMATE_SAMPLE)]
    formatted = _encoded_size(
        ";\n\n".join(
            sqlparse.format(str(statement), reindent=True, keyword_case="upper")
            for statement in sample
        )
    )

    return int(formatted * total / len(sample))

Store serialized dictionaries as local directory trees.

A serialized dictionary mixes JSON-supported primitives with files and nested containers. This module turns such a dictionary into a directory tree and back:

  • primitives are collected in a __index__.yaml file inside the directory,
  • files are written next to it, named by their key,
  • nested dictionaries and lists become sub-directories named by their key,
  • the __index__.yaml of a list directory holds a YAML list, with None at the positions taken by files or sub-directories, and the files in that directory are named by their position.

def read_structure(path: Path | str) -> SerializedDict:
    """Read a local directory tree back into a serialized dictionary.

    Primitive values come from ``__index__.yaml``, files are returned as
    :class:`LocalFile` handles, and sub-directories are read recursively.

def write_structure(structure: SerializedDict, path: Path | str) -> LocalDir:

    The directory is created when it does not exist. Entries are overwritten by
    key, and an entry whose key changes shape (a file replaced by a
    sub-directory, or the other way round) replaces the old artifact instead of
    being overlaid on it. Entries that the structure no longer mentions at all

    does not delete anything.

        path: The directory to write into.

    Returns:
        The directory that was written.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a key is not a valid entry name, or would take the name of

    _write_node(structure, directory)

@staticmethod
def from_instance[I](instance: I) -> TypeRef[I]:
    """Get the type associated with this instance, may be generic.

    Args:
        instance: The instance to get type for.

    Returns:
        The type associated with the instance.
    """
    if hasattr(instance, "__orig_class__"):
        orig_class = getattr(instance, "__orig_class__")
        typ = TypeRef(orig_class).exact_type_node

def is_subtype_of(self, supertype: TypeDef[T] | TypeForm[T]) -> TypeGuard[TypeForm[T]]:
    """Check if this type reference is a subtype of the given type hint.

    Args:
        supertype: The supertype to check against.

    super_typeref = TypeRef(supertype)

    try:
        return is_subhint(
            cast(Any, self.runtime_type_def),
            cast(Any, super_typeref.runtime_type_def),

            issubclass(t, tuple(super_typeref.typeset)) for t in self.typeset
        )

def validate(self, obj: Any, with_attrs: bool = True) -> TypeGuard[T]:
    """Check if object is of this type.

    The runtime check is performed with beartype. ``Annotated`` metadata that
    carries pydantic validation (a ``FieldInfo`` or an object implementing the
    core-schema hook) is enforced as well; a failed validation yields ``False``
    rather than raising.

    Args:
        obj: The object to check.
        with_attrs: Whether to validate attributes by their annotations.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if the object is of this type, ``False`` otherwise.
    """
    if isinstance(obj, Runtyped):
        return is_subtype(type(obj), self.runtime_type_def)

    if not is_bearable(obj, cast(Any, self.runtime_type_def)):
        return False

    if isinstance(self.runtime_type_def, RuntimeValidated) or any(
        isinstance(a, RuntimeValidated | FieldInfo) for a in self.annotations
    ):
        try:
            TypeAdapter(self.runtime_type_def).validate_python(obj)
        except ValidationError:
            return False

    if with_attrs and self.attr_typehints is not None:
        if not _validate_attrs(obj, self.attr_typehints):
            return False

    return True

def get_inheritance_distance(cls: type, base: type) -> int | None:
    """Return the inheritance distance between two classes.

    Note: Positive direction is from subclass to base class. If arguments are
    are reversed, the sign will be negative.

    Warning: Untested function.

    Args:
        cls: The subclass.
        base: The base class.

    Returns:
        The signed inheritance distance between the two classes. If the base class is
        not a base of the subclass, None is returned.
    """
    if not isinstance(cls, type) or not isinstance(base, type):
        return None

    if cls is base:
        return 0

    if issubclass(cls, base):
        cls, base, sign = (cls, base, 1)
    elif issubclass(base, cls):
        cls, base, sign = (base, cls, -1)
    else:
        return None

    distance = 1
    bases = set(cls.__bases__)
    while base not in bases and distance < 100:
        bases = reduce(set.union, (set(b.__bases__) for b in bases))
        distance += 1

    return distance * sign

def get_lowest_common_base(types: Iterable[type]) -> type:
    """Return the lowest common base of given types.

    Args:
        types: The types to get the common base for.

    Returns:
        The lowest common base type.
    """
    type_list = list(types)
    if len(type_list) == 0:
        return object

    bases_of_all = reduce(set.intersection, (set(getmro(t)) for t in type_list))
    return max(bases_of_all, key=lambda b: sum(issubclass(b, t) for t in bases_of_all))

def get_nondefault_methods(cls: type) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Get the all attributes on a class without those inherited from ``object``.

    Args:
        cls: The class to get methods for.

    Returns:
        Mapping of method names to method objects.
    """
    return {
        name: member
        for name, member in inspect.getmembers(
            cls,
            predicate=lambda m: (
                inspect.ismethoddescriptor(m) or inspect.isfunction(m) or inspect.isbuiltin(m)
            ),
        )
        if not (
            (
                inspect.getmodule(member) is None
                and str(member.__qualname__).startswith("object" + ".")
            )
            or name == "__subclasshook__"
        )
    }

def get_own_attrs(
    cls: type,
    predicate: Callable[[object], bool] | None = None,
    include_bases: tuple[type, ...] = (),
) -> set[str]:
    """Get all non-inherited attributes on a class.

    Args:
        cls: The class to get attributes for.
        predicate: Optional predicate to filter attributes.
        include_bases: Additional base classes to include attributes from.

    Returns:
        Set of attribute names.
    """
    if predicate is None:
        attrs = set(cls.__dict__.keys())
        attrs.update(getattr(cls, "__annotations__", {}).keys())
    else:
        attrs = {name for name, value in cls.__dict__.items() if predicate(value)}

    included_cls_mods = [
        supcls
        for base in include_bases
        for supcls in (base, *get_subclasses(base))
        if issubclass(cls, supcls) and supcls is not cls
    ]
    sup_attrs = reduce(
        set.__or__,
        (
            get_own_attrs(
                supcls,
                predicate=predicate,
                include_bases=(),
            )
            for supcls in included_cls_mods
        ),
        set(),
    )

    return sup_attrs | attrs

def is_immutable(obj: Any) -> bool:
    """Check if an object is immutable.

    Args:
        obj: The object to check.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if the object is immutable.
    """
    # Built-in immutables
    if isinstance(obj, int | float | bool | str | bytes | frozenset):
        return True

    # Tuples: check recursively
    if isinstance(obj, tuple):
        return all(is_immutable(el) for el in obj)

    # Frozen dataclass
    if is_frozen_dataclass(obj):
        return True

    return False

def is_type_hint[T](obj: TypeForm[T] | T) -> TypeGuard[TypeForm[T]]:
    """Check whether an object is a type hint rather than a value.

    Classes, unions, named aliases, parameterized generics and any hint with an
    origin count as type hints; instances, strings and numbers do not.

    Args:
        obj: The object to check.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if ``obj`` describes a type instead of being a value of one.
    """
    return (
        isinstance(obj, type | UnionType | TypeAliasType | TypeVar | TypeVarTuple | ForwardRef)
        or isinstance(obj, GenericAlias)
        or get_origin(obj) is not None
    )
